paragraphs.heading: Prepare your small group leaders
paragraphs.edited: So I would encourage you to maybe do that this week, or to find a way to incorporate many questions into your large group time. Then, during small group time, you can drill those questions down a little bit deeper. But make sure, as you do that, that your small group leaders are adequately prepared to handle some of the questions. Based on your situation and the leadership you have in place and the volunteers you have in place, just make sure that they are equipped to properly answer. paragraphs.heading: This week's storyteller
paragraphs.edited: Another important, powerful tool is your storyteller this week. To have somebody in front of your students who has actually expressed doubt and walked through it in some way, shape or form can be incredibly important. That story, whatever they've been through, will resonate, I'm sure, with many of your students. So make sure you know that you don't need to find the best story or the biggest story or the most compelling story — just something that lets students see, "Hey, I'm not the only one going through this. I'm not the only student dealing with this. I'm not the only person who has ever dealt with this, and people have gotten through it."

paragraphs.heading: God can handle it
paragraphs.edited: Because some students might just have little questions here and there. Other students might be at a significant crisis of faith in their lives, where they need serious direction. And after all that you've gone through in this study, some of those things may start to come up to the surface a little bit. So remind your students that no matter their questions, no matter their doubts, God can handle it, and that He has given us everything we need to be entirely confident of who He is, who Jesus is, and what our salvation means.
